IGF1-LR3 is a scam. PT2. #igf1lr3 #bodybuilding #looksmaxing  #peptide #hgh                                       IGF1-LR3 was created specifically to avoid IGF binding proteins. This was done to study IGF1's direct effect on cells that aren't facilitated through IGF1BP's (igf1 binding proteins) which IGF1 usually binds to. This made it look significantly more potent than it is in real world scenarios, because igfl-lr3 could interact with the receptor directly in vitro, but the human body is much more complex. Because IGF1-LR3 avoids IGF binding proteins, it can freely bind to receptors in vitro, making it look very potent. However, we are humans, not a petri dish. IGFBPs + ALS (which IGF1-LR3 avoids) are REQUIRED for proper transport, stability, and regulated delivery to tissues like bone and muscle. Without these carrier proteins igf1/igf1-Ir3 is degraded within minutes, not being able to reach muscle and bone tissue which need prolonged signaling for growth. IGF binding proteins don't just act as a carrier for IGF1, its required for correct positioning at the cell surface so the receptor gets a focused and sustained signal. Don't think of IGF binding proteins as the equivalent to SHBG, it couldn't be further from the truth. SHBG binds to circulating androgens and other hormones and prevents them from reaching receptors, rendering them inactive. IGBP's do the opposite and transport/regulate igfl's binding, and protect IGF1 from being degraded within minutes. MYTH: "IGF1-LR3 doesn't need these binding proteins because it has a half life of 20-30 hours so it can sustainably signal tissue." The counter point to this is simple: There is literally no evidence that IGF1-LR3 has a half life of 20-30 hours. In fact we have contrary evidence (although in rats) that igf-Ir3 isn't detectable at all within 4 hours of administration, suggesting an extremely low half life. ( - PMID: 33587816 A lot of people will claim that this debunking is BS because they "felt" IGF1-LR3, these effects are real (in some users) and actually potentiated through Ir3's strong initial glucose changes (which is the only thing its good at), creating a feeling of feeling more pumped, warmer, or fuller after carbs, but this doesn't mean growth. IGF1-LR3 is useless because it cannot effectively target and signal IGF1 receptors due to its inability to bind to essential carrier proteins, making it degrade in minutes. Your brain on armodafinil is literally running 5 different upgrades at the same time. Here’s what’s actually happening inside your skull 🧠⚡ Most people think it’s just “a stronger coffee.” They are so wrong it’s almost funny. Armodafinil isn’t caffeine. It isn’t Adderall. It operates on completely different pathways — and once you understand the mechanism, you’ll get why people call it the cleanest focus compound ever studied. Let’s break down what’s actually going on. First, the basics. Modafinil is a mix of two mirror-image molecules. Armodafinil is just the active one — the R-enantiomer. Longer half-life (~15hrs vs ~12hrs), smoother plasma levels all day, cleaner cognitive effect. It’s like going from a flip phone to a flagship. Same concept, completely different performance. Now here’s where it gets interesting 👇 Pathway 1 — Dopamine (but not how you think) Armodafinil doesn’t flood your brain with dopamine like amphetamines do. It blocks the DAT transporter — the protein that “vacuums up” dopamine after it’s done signalling. So dopamine that was already being released naturally just… stays around longer. Smooth, sustained elevation. No spike. No crash. No depleted reserves. That’s the entire reason there’s no comedown. Pathway 2 — Norepinephrine (your urgency signal) This one hits different. Norepinephrine in the prefrontal cortex basically tells your brain “THIS matters, pay attention NOW.” It filters out background noise and directs all your processing toward whatever is in front of you. The hippocampus — your memory filing system — is packed with norepinephrine receptors. When it’s elevated during studying, it acts like a biological highlighter, tagging incoming info as worth storing long-term. What you learn actually sticks instead of fading in 9 hours. Pathway 3 — Orexin (the real reason there’s no crash) Caffeine works by blocking adenosine — the tiredness chemical that builds up all day. The problem? The adenosine never stops accumulating. When caffeine wears off, all of it hits at once. That IS the crash. Armodafinil doesn’t touch adenosine at all. Instead it activates the orexin system — the hypothalamus neurons that ARE the brain’s wakefulness switch. It generates alertness at the source. No borrowed energy. Nothing to pay back later. Pathway 4 — Histamine (whole brain alertness) Most people don’t know histamine does anything in the brain. In reality it’s one of the primary signals keeping your cortex switched on. That drowsiness you feel after antihistamines? That’s this exact pathway being shut off. Armodafinil drives it the other direction — increases histamine release brain-wide. And because orexin neurons directly connect to and excite the histamine system, activating orexin automatically triggers this as a downstream effect. One compound, compounding effects. Pathway 5 — Glutamate & Memory Formation The final piece. Glutamate is the brain’s primary excitatory neurotransmitter and the molecule most directly responsible for learning at a cellular level. Armodafinil indirectly increases glutamate activity while reducing GABA (the inhibitory brake). This shifts neural circuits toward excitation — neurons fire more readily, communicate more efficiently, form new connections more easily. Memory formation (long-term potentiation) is directly triggered by glutamate acting on NMDA receptors. Lower that threshold and new information is more likely to produce actual structural changes in your brain, not just temporary short-term retention. Key Takeaways 🔑 🧪 Armodafinil = the purified, longer-lasting version of modafinil ⚡ Blocks DAT → sustained dopamine without a crash 🎯 Orexin activation = wakefulness without borrowed energy 🧬 Norepinephrine tags memories as important during learning 🔗 All 5 pathways compound and reinforce each other simultaneously #educational #nootropics #neuroscience #studytok #looksmax

This video is meant as an educational warning about the risks of mixing prescription medications in social or recreational settings. A lot of people talk online about “stacks,” “party hacks,” or ways to stay awake, reduce anxiety, or feel more social — but combining medicines without proper medical guidance can be dangerous, unpredictable, and in some cases life-threatening. The problem with medication combinations is that each compound can affect the brain and body in a different way. Some medicines can increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, lower blood pressure, or impair coordination. Others can mask those effects temporarily, which may make someone feel more functional while actually increasing the risk of overdoing it, blacking out, falling, or making unsafe decisions. What looks like a clever shortcut can quickly become a medical emergency. This video is not meant to encourage self-experimentation, recreational drug use, or “biohacking” with prescription products. It is also not medical advice. The goal is to show why it is risky to treat medicines like tools for partying, studying, or pushing through a night out. Even when a drug is legally prescribed to someone, that does not mean it is safe to combine with other substances or use in a different context. Many online posts present medication combinations in a confident, almost persuasive way. That can create a false sense of safety. In reality, the effects depend on a person’s health, age, dose, tolerance, other medications, alcohol use, sleep deprivation, and many other factors. Two people can take the same substances and have very different reactions. A combination that seems “fine” for one person can be dangerous for another. If you are taking any prescription medication, the safest move is to ask a licensed doctor or pharmacist before combining it with anything else, including alcohol, energy drinks, sleep aids, anxiety medications, or substances used recreationally. Never assume that a compound is safe just because it is common, discussed online, or used by other people. Social media is not a substitute for medical guidance. This video is also a reminder that side effects can happen fast. Warning signs may include unusual sleepiness, dizziness, confusion, vomiting, trouble breathing, fainting, slurred speech, chest pain, or behavior that seems out of character. If someone becomes difficult to wake, has slowed breathing, collapses, or seems medically unwell after mixing substances, treat it seriously and get emergency help immediately. A lot of harm starts when people normalize risky combinations because they are described as useful, efficient, or “low-key.” But the body does not care about internet trends. The safe approach is to respect the fact that prescription medicines are designed for specific medical purposes, not for boosting nights out or forcing extra productivity. If a medication is causing side effects, the right answer is not to pile on more drugs to cancel them out — it is to speak to a professional. Please use this video as a cautionary example, not a blueprint. If you or someone you know is considering combining medications, get advice from a doctor or pharmacist first. If someone is already unwell after taking something, do not wait for it to “wear off” if symptoms are severe. Safety first, always. Educational only. Not medical advice. Do not combine prescription medicines without professional guidance. #educational #looksmax #pharma #slaying #nightout

This video breaks down BAM15, a mitochondrial uncoupler that is currently being studied in preclinical research as a potential pharma candidate for combating obesity. The core idea is that it does what DNP does, which is force your mitochondria to burn through energy without producing ATP efficiently, essentially turning your body into a furnace that runs hot and burns through fat stores at an accelerated rate. But the critical difference is in how precisely it does this and where in the body it ends up, which is what makes it so interesting from a research perspective. The main problem with DNP, which has killed people, is that it accumulates in the brainstem, cardiac tissue, and the hypothalamus because of how it moves through the body. When you push the dose high enough to see real fat loss, it starts uncoupling heat generation in the exact tissues responsible for regulating your core body temperature, which is how people die from overheating. BAM15 has a carboxylic acid group that keeps it ionized at physiological pH, which means it partitions poorly into the blood-brain barrier and instead concentrates in highly perfused oxidative tissues like skeletal muscle and brown adipose tissue. That is precisely where you want the thermogenesis happening, and it is why the safety window is estimated to be around ten times wider than DNP in preclinical data. Beyond just burning more energy as heat, BAM15 also activates a cascade through AMPK, which lowers malonyl-CoA levels and releases the brake on CPT1a, the enzyme that shuttles long-chain fatty acids into the mitochondrial system. This means your cells start actively hunting and oxidizing free fatty acids while sparing glycogen, which is the opposite of what stimulant-based pharma like amphetamines or ephedrine does. Those compounds mobilize fat from adipocytes through adrenaline but do nothing to ensure those released fatty acids actually get oxidized. BAM15 closes that gap, which is why the fatty acid oxidation rate shown in the video is roughly 77% higher than DNP and nearly 180% higher than clenbuterol in the comparison data. On top of the fat oxidation angle, the video also explains how BAM15 upregulates glucose disposal in skeletal muscle through a parallel AMPK-mediated pathway that triggers GLUT4 translocation to the sarcolemma completely independently of insulin. This means blood glucose gets cleared into muscle even when insulin signaling is blunted or absent, which is a big deal for anyone dealing with insulin resistance or just trying to manage their blood sugar response after high-carb meals. Most stimulants actually blunt this process by raising cortisol and promoting peripheral insulin resistance, so the contrast is meaningful. The preclinical mouse data referenced shows a 21.67% reduction in total body weight over 10 weeks in aged obese mice at the 85mg/kg/day dose, with no observed deaths and no hyperthermia or lactic acidosis at effective doses. The video makes it clear this is animal model data only, that human trials do not exist yet, and that the FDA would typically start clinical dosing at around one tenth of the human equivalent dose for a mechanistically potent compound like this. It is a genuinely interesting research compound, and the video frames it as something worth watching as it moves toward clinical development. Educational only.
